summary: Macro template regression caused SLA routing alerts and monthly SLA report drift
description:
Issue summary: A recent change to the support macro templating engine unintentionally stripped the SLA routing tags that downstream routing rules rely on. Impact: automated escalation and SLA metering for internal queues is misattributed, causing false P0/P1 alerts to paging and corrupting the daily and monthly SLA reports for the support org. Environment: production support-tooling cluster (us-east) and the reporting pipeline ingesting alerting events.

Observed impact:
- On 2026-03-12 07:10 UTC, multiple internal pages were created for support queues that should have been routed to the Dedicated SRE rotation. Those pages were instead routed to the general #support-ops rota.
- Upstream analytics shows a ~42% drop in routed SLA-tagged events between 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC and 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC.
- The nightly SLA aggregation job produced a monthly report with missing SLA rows for four internal queues.

Steps to reproduce (attempted):
1) Create a support ticket via the internal UI using template 'DEDICATED-ESCALATE-v2' in prod/us-east.
2) Observe the generated ticket payload in the support-tooling queue (support-events topic).
3) Confirm whether the sla_tag and routing_policy fields are present in the payload.

Expected behavior: macro templates preserve required metadata fields (sla_tag, routing_policy, customer_tier) in generated payloads.
Actual behavior: sla_tag and routing_policy are empty strings in 100% of reproduced tickets when template rendering uses the new template engine version.

Immediate mitigation applied: we rolled back the template-engine to v1.17 at 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC which restored normal routing for newly created tickets. Historical events from 2026-03-11 21:00 UTC to 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC still require remediation in the reporting ingestion layer.

Business impact: internal paging fatigue due to duplicate/false pages, inaccurate SLA reporting for leadership, and potential missed escalations for Dedicated and Private customer queues. This is an internal-support incident but could affect SLA dashboards used by GTM and CSM teams.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 07:45 UTC - Support observed first anomalous routing; alerting noise increased on #support-ops (reported by Priya Patel).
2026-03-12 08:10 UTC - Platform Observability confirmed drop in SLA-tagged events via packet of Kibana queries (see dashboard SLO-Routing-Overview).
2026-03-12 09:00 UTC - Reproduced locally: template-renderer v2.3 returns empty strings for sla_tag when optional context keys are unset. Reproduction steps recorded and attached to the PR thread.

2026-03-12 09:40 UTC - Hypothesis: a change in the template engine's handling of null/undefined variables (introduced in template-engine v2.3) removed default tag insertion logic from our macro building layer.
2026-03-12 10:05 UTC - Rolled back template-engine to v1.17 in prod, confirmed routing restored for new tickets. Rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/support-tooling/pull/423
2026-03-12 13:30 UTC - Began bulk remediation plan for historical events: mark-and-reprocess pipeline to inject missing SLA tags for events in the 2026-03-11 21:00 to 2026-03-12 10:05 window.
2026-03-13 09:15 UTC - Data team completed a dry-run on a staging subset (5000 events) and confirmed idempotent reprocessing preserves ticket creation timestamps and incident links.
2026-03-14 08:00 UTC - Preparing rollout of reprocessing job to backfill production events; scheduled for 2026-03-14 23:00 UTC with a feature-flag-controlled run.

next_steps: Run backfill job 2026-03-14 23:00 UTC under feature flag; monitor SLO-Routing-Overview and paging noise for 2 hours post-run.
Add a regression unit test to support-tooling that ensures sla_tag and routing_policy default behavior across template-engine versions (owner: platform-engineering).
Patch template-engine v2.x to restore default tag insertion semantics and release as v2.3.1 with compatibility tests (owner: infra-dev).
Create a one-off report to regenerate monthly SLA rows for the affected date range and notify GTM/CSM when reports are updated (owner: analytics).
Follow-up postmortem and change in deployment gating: require a support-tooling integration test job that exercises routing and reporting templates before any template-engine upgrades (owner: SRE).
resolution: In progress - rollback restored immediate behavior; backfill scheduled. Final resolution pending successful backfill and a compatibility patch to template-engine. Postmortem and follow-up actions to be published to Confluence after incident closure.
resolution_notes: Rollback performed (v2.3 -> v1.17) at 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC. Backfill scheduled 2026-03-14 23:00 UTC. Data dry-run passed on staging. Patch PR for template-engine compatibility in review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/support-tooling/pull/427.
customer_impact: Internal-only (support queues). Potential downstream impact to GTM dashboards if historical reports are not backfilled before 2026-03-15.
postmortem_pointer: will be created at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/POSTMORTEM-INT-9987 after incident closure
